title: Even God wants a blessing (Berakhot 7a)
hook: the high priest Ishmael is asked by God for a blessing, and blesses God with mercy
tomorrow: where does God live when the Temple is gone?

segments.voice: Yesterday, God prays: may My mercy overcome My anger. Same page, next story. That prayer gets said back to God, by a person.

A whiff of cinnamon, and you're back in somebody's kitchen years ago, before you've even placed it. Berakhot's next story begins inside a cloud of smell: incense, in the innermost room of the Temple, where a priest has come in alone. And in that smoke, God asks him for a blessing.
screen: `A WHIFF OF CINNAMON.` → `INCENSE IN THE INNERMOST ROOM.` → `GOD ASKS FOR A BLESSING.`

segments.voice: Rabbi Ishmael son of Elisha tells it himself. Once I went into the innermost sanctum to offer incense, and I saw Akatriel Yah, the LORD of hosts, seated on a high and lifted throne. And He said to me: Ishmael, My son, bless Me. Stop there. The LORD of hosts asks a human being for a blessing. What does Ishmael say? He gives back yesterday's prayer: may it be Your will that Your mercy conquer Your anger, that Your mercy prevail over Your other ways, that You deal with Your children with mercy, beyond the letter of the law. And God nodded His head to him. A nod, in the smoke. Then the Talmud draws the lesson: don't let the blessing of an ordinary person be light in your eyes. If God wanted Ishmael's, an ordinary blessing counts. Here's one to tell a friend tonight: in the Talmud, God asks a priest for a blessing, and answers it with a nod. So blessing doesn't only flow down, from the great to the small. It can rise. A child can bless a parent, a student a teacher, a person God. Bless the one above.
screen: `ISHMAEL, MY SON, BLESS ME.` · `MAY YOUR MERCY CONQUER YOUR ANGER.` · `GOD NODS.` · `NO BLESSING IS LIGHT.` · then, large: `BLESS THE ONE ABOVE.`

segments.voice: If there's a spice jar, a tea bag or a candle within reach, hold it close and breathe in slowly; if not, call up the smell of something warm. Let the scent bring you to one person above you, a parent, a teacher, a boss, an elder. For the rest of the sit, wish them one good thing, in your own words.
screen: `ONE SCENT.` · `ONE PERSON ABOVE YOU.` · `ONE GOOD WISH.`

segments.voice: Even God wants a blessing. Rabbi Ishmael, asked by God to bless, blesses God with mercy, and God nods.
screen: `EVEN GOD WANTS A BLESSING — today's word`.

segments.voice: Something to keep: bless the one above, and never call a small blessing light. Berakhot, day eight.

screen: `DAY 1495 COUNTS.` → `BERAKHOT · 8 OF 50.` → `TOMORROW: WHERE DOES GOD LIVE WHEN THE TEMPLE IS GONE?`
